window-cleaning.alt: Two-storey waterfront home with large windows along a covered porch
window-cleaning.caption: The property in Bow, Skagit County. Glass facing salt water is a different job from glass ten miles inland.

window-cleaning.alt: Green-framed glass door and sidelight before cleaning, webs and dirt along the frames
window-cleaning.caption: Before. Webs and debris collect in the frame channels, not only on the glass, which is why frames and tracks are part of the job.

window-cleaning.alt: Bank of green-framed waterfront windows before cleaning, hazy with salt spray
window-cleaning.caption: Before. Salt haze does not rinse off in the rain — it has to be washed off, or it keeps dulling the view.

window-cleaning.alt: Large waterfront window before cleaning, heavy streaking and salt residue clouding the view
window-cleaning.caption: Before. The streaking is mineral residue left behind as salt spray dries on the pane.

window-cleaning.alt: Water-fed pole reaching upper gable windows to scrub and rinse them from the ground
window-cleaning.caption: Upper gable glass reached from the ground. Purified water means nothing is left on the pane as it dries.

window-cleaning.alt: The same waterfront window after cleaning, clear glass and an unobstructed view to the water
window-cleaning.caption: After, same pane.

window-cleaning.alt: Bank of green-framed windows after cleaning, glass and frames clear
window-cleaning.caption: After, same bank of windows.

window-cleaning.alt: Green-framed glass door after cleaning, free of webs and debris
window-cleaning.caption: After, same door. Frames and sill cleared as well as the glass.

window-cleaning.alt: Long pole brush cleaning large multi-pane windows on a house with green trim
window-cleaning.caption: Multi-pane glass takes longer than the pane count suggests — every bar is an edge to work around.

window-cleaning.alt: Technician using a long pole to reach upper windows of a two-storey house
window-cleaning.caption: Second-storey glass without putting a ladder on soft ground or decking.

window-cleaning.alt: Technician on a ladder cleaning an arched second-storey window on a gray-sided house
window-cleaning.caption: Where a pole cannot do it properly, the ladder comes out and gets footed correctly.

window-cleaning.alt: Technician using a long pole to clean large triangular windows of a house with green trim
window-cleaning.caption: Gable triangles are the panes most often skipped by a cheaper quote.

window-cleaning.alt: Technician rinsing second-floor windows of a two-storey home from the ground
window-cleaning.caption: Rinsing down from the top so nothing dries on the glass below.

window-cleaning.alt: Technician using a squeegee to clean a soapy window from inside, water view beyond
window-cleaning.caption: Interiors are half the job on a view property, and the half people notice from the sofa.

window-cleaning.alt: Long pole with a squeegee reaching a high triangular window framed by timber beams
window-cleaning.caption: A Ferndale home. Vaulted rooms put the dirtiest glass where nobody can reach it.

gutter-cleaning.alt: Gloved hand holding a large clump of wet organic debris pulled from a gutter
gutter-cleaning.caption: A Bellingham home. Gutters here fill with fir needles rather than leaves, and needles pack into a mat water cannot pass.

gutter-cleaning.alt: Handful of wet leaves and fir needles lifted out of a gutter above a deck
gutter-cleaning.caption: Cleared by hand and bagged rather than flushed down the downpipe — which is how a clear gutter ends up with a blocked drain.

gutter-cleaning.alt: Roof valley and gutter line after accumulated needles and debris were removed
gutter-cleaning.caption: The valley matters as much as the gutter: debris held there keeps the shingles underneath permanently damp.

gutter-cleaning.alt: Cleared gutter channel running along a roofline with an open path for water
gutter-cleaning.caption: After. Bellingham.

gutter-cleaning.alt: Gutter run clear of needles and debris with an open path toward the downspout
gutter-cleaning.caption: The test is not that it looks clean — it is that water has an unbroken path to the downpipe.

gutter-cleaning.alt: Gutter and roof edge filled with fallen autumn leaves
gutter-cleaning.caption: What a gutter looks like when it is already past overflowing.

gutter-cleaning.alt: Gloved hand removing packed debris from a clogged gutter
gutter-cleaning.caption: Ferndale. Leaves, moss and grit compact into a plug that water runs straight over.

gutter-cleaning.alt: Close-up of a gray asphalt shingle roof meeting the gutter line
gutter-cleaning.caption: Sedro-Woolley. The roof edge and the gutter are one system, and they silt up together.

gutter-cleaning.alt: Gutter packed with fir needles and roof debris before the roof was cleared
gutter-cleaning.caption: Before. Under forest cover the roof and the gutter fill together, so they are one job rather than two.

gutter-cleaning.alt: Asphalt roof and gutter line covered in needles, leaves and organic debris
gutter-cleaning.caption: Before. A gutter in this state does not drip — it overflows at the back edge, behind the fascia.

gutter-cleaning.alt: Roof edge and gutter cleared of debris, with the shingle surface exposed
gutter-cleaning.caption: After, same roof edge.

roof-cleaning.alt: Steep gray shingled roof being rinsed with a low-pressure stream of water
roof-cleaning.caption: Rinsing down a steep pitch from the ridge, worked from a ladder rather than from the shingles.

roof-cleaning.alt: Shingled roof being sprayed with a low-pressure stream from a hose
roof-cleaning.caption: The only pressure a composition roof should ever see.

roof-cleaning.alt: High-angle view along a shingle roof ridge with a vent pipe, water beyond
roof-cleaning.caption: Composition shingle with the growth taken off it. The granules are the wearing surface and they do not grow back.

roof-cleaning.alt: Long pole spraying water to remove moss from an asphalt shingle roof
roof-cleaning.caption: Worked from the ground where the pitch allows it.

roof-cleaning.alt: Thick moss growth covering asphalt roof shingles
roof-cleaning.caption: Moss this established has already lifted the shingle edges it is growing under.

roof-cleaning.alt: View from a roof over the shingles to a work truck in the driveway below
roof-cleaning.caption: The view from the job. Ladders, hoses and tanks travel with the crew.

roof-cleaning.alt: Asphalt roof buried under thick moss, needles and forest debris before treatment
roof-cleaning.caption: Before, Sedro-Woolley. This is what a shaded roof does under forest cover here.

roof-cleaning.alt: Two skylights almost buried under leaves, needles and moss before the roof was cleared
roof-cleaning.caption: Before. Both skylights are under there.

roof-cleaning.alt: Gloved hand holding a thick clump of moss and organic debris lifted off a roof
roof-cleaning.caption: Moss comes off by hand and at low pressure. A pressure washer takes the shingle granules with it.

roof-cleaning.alt: Roof partway through moss removal, cleared shingles on one side and growth remaining on the other
roof-cleaning.caption: Halfway across, which is the clearest look at what was actually on the roof.

moss-removal.alt: Asphalt roof buried under thick moss, needles and forest debris before treatment
moss-removal.caption: Before, Sedro-Woolley. This is what a shaded roof does under forest cover here.

moss-removal.alt: Two skylights almost buried under leaves, needles and moss before the roof was cleared
moss-removal.caption: Before. Both skylights are under there.

moss-removal.alt: Gloved hand holding a thick clump of moss and organic debris lifted off a roof
moss-removal.caption: Moss comes off by hand and at low pressure. A pressure washer takes the shingle granules with it.

moss-removal.alt: Roof partway through moss removal, cleared shingles on one side and growth remaining on the other
moss-removal.caption: Halfway across, which is the clearest look at what was actually on the roof.

moss-removal.alt: Roof ridge after the bulk moss and debris were removed, with the shingles visible again
moss-removal.caption: After. Same roof as the first photograph in this run.

moss-removal.alt: The same skylights after debris removal, fully exposed on a cleared roof
moss-removal.caption: After, same skylights.

moss-removal.alt: Applying a roof-safe treatment across cleared shingles after the bulk moss was removed
moss-removal.caption: Clearing the moss is half of it. The treatment is what slows it coming back.

moss-removal.alt: Asphalt roof after a roof-safe powder moss treatment was applied along the ridge
moss-removal.caption: Powder along the ridge; rain carries it down the slope over the following weeks.

moss-removal.alt: Asphalt shingles after debris removal, with previously hidden moss growth now visible
moss-removal.caption: The debris came off and the moss underneath was still there — which is the problem with clearing without treating.

metal-roof-soft-washing.alt: Green standing-seam metal roof on a stone home before cleaning, dulled by organic growth
metal-roof-soft-washing.caption: Before, Whatcom County. The green finish is still under there; what you see is growth sitting on the coating.

metal-roof-soft-washing.alt: Standing-seam metal roof inspected and assessed before a low-pressure soft wash
metal-roof-soft-washing.caption: Assessed before anything is applied — coating condition decides what the roof can take.

metal-roof-soft-washing.alt: Ladder set up beside a stone home for access to the metal roof
metal-roof-soft-washing.caption: Access set up off the roof itself. Walking a wet standing-seam panel is how people fall and how panels dent.

metal-roof-soft-washing.alt: Technician protecting siding, windows and planting before soft washing a roof
metal-roof-soft-washing.caption: What goes on before the first drop: everything below the work gets covered or rinsed.

metal-roof-soft-washing.alt: Soft wash solution applied at low pressure to a corrugated metal roof
metal-roof-soft-washing.caption: Low pressure and the right chemistry. Pressure strips coatings off metal, which is a repaint rather than a clean.

metal-roof-soft-washing.alt: Standing-seam metal roof after a low-pressure soft wash, clean and reflective
metal-roof-soft-washing.caption: After. Nothing was recoated — that is the original finish with the growth taken off it.

metal-roof-soft-washing.alt: The stone home's metal roof after cleaning, with the green finish restored
metal-roof-soft-washing.caption: After, from the same position as the first photograph in this run.

house-washing.alt: White lap siding before washing, with green organic growth across the lower courses
house-washing.caption: Before, a Lynden home. Growth starts low and on the shaded side, where the wall stays damp longest.

house-washing.alt: Long exterior wall of a home before washing, dulled by organic buildup
house-washing.caption: Before. From here it reads as "the paint has aged", which is usually growth rather than age.

house-washing.alt: Close-up of heavy green and dark organic staining embedded on white siding
house-washing.caption: Close up, it is clearly biological — and it is in the surface, not on it.

house-washing.alt: Technician applying a siding-safe soft wash solution to an upper wall
house-washing.caption: Applied from the ground. Water driven behind a lap board has to come out somewhere.

house-washing.alt: Technician soft washing the exterior wall of a home from the lawn at low pressure
house-washing.caption: Siding gets washed, not blasted.

house-washing.alt: Side wall of a home before washing, with organic discoloration along the siding
house-washing.caption: Before, the shaded side wall.

house-washing.alt: The same side wall after soft washing, the white siding clean and uniform
house-washing.caption: After, same wall, same day.

house-washing.alt: Close-up of lap siding before treatment, showing green organic growth across several boards
house-washing.caption: Before, close enough to count the courses.

house-washing.alt: Close-up of lap siding after soft washing, clean and free of organic growth
house-washing.caption: After, same boards.

house-washing.alt: The same long exterior wall after washing, with bright, clean siding
house-washing.caption: After. Same wall as the second photograph in this run.

house-washing.alt: Rinsing red board-and-batten siding on a two-storey home
house-washing.caption: Board-and-batten on another Whatcom County property. The battens hold debris along every vertical seam.

house-washing.alt: Close-up of clean cream lap siding at a corner board after a house washing
house-washing.caption: Corner boards and trim are where a rushed house wash shows.

pressure-washing.alt: Large concrete area in front of a home, darkened almost black by organic growth
pressure-washing.caption: Before, Mount Vernon. Concrete goes black here from organic growth, not dirt — which is why sweeping never touches it.

pressure-washing.alt: Concrete before cleaning, showing the extent of dark organic contamination
pressure-washing.caption: Before, the front entry. Black concrete is biological, and biological is what makes it slick underfoot.

pressure-washing.alt: Technician running a surface cleaner across a driveway beside the branded company truck
pressure-washing.caption: The truck carries its own water, tanks and power, so a job does not depend on the tap at the property.

pressure-washing.alt: Technician running a professional surface cleaner across concrete beside the company truck
pressure-washing.caption: A surface cleaner rather than a wand, so there are no stripes left across the slab.

pressure-washing.alt: Concrete walkway showing the contrast between a cleaned section and darker untreated concrete
pressure-washing.caption: Mid-job on the walkway. The line is the honest measure of what was on the surface.

pressure-washing.alt: The concrete walkway after cleaning, organic growth and dark staining removed
pressure-washing.caption: After. A walkway that goes black also goes slippery, which is the part that matters in a wet winter.

pressure-washing.alt: Front entry and concrete after pressure washing, visibly brighter and more uniform
pressure-washing.caption: After, the front entry.

pressure-washing.alt: Garage driveway after pressure washing, with an even, clean concrete surface
pressure-washing.caption: After, the driveway.

pressure-washing.alt: Black work truck loaded with ladders, hose reels and cleaning equipment
pressure-washing.caption: Parked up on a job. Everything needed for a day of work travels on the truck.

solar-panel-cleaning.alt: Wide view of a 128-panel commercial solar array on a flat rooftop
solar-panel-cleaning.caption: A 128-panel commercial array. Output is measurable, so on a roof this size so is the cost of leaving it dirty.

solar-panel-cleaning.alt: Rows of solar panels coated in dirt, dust and water spotting before cleaning
solar-panel-cleaning.caption: Before. Panels do not need to look filthy to be down on output.

solar-panel-cleaning.alt: Close-up of a solar panel showing heavy dirt, pollen and bird droppings on the glass
solar-panel-cleaning.caption: Pollen, dust and droppings. Any of it shades cells, and shaded cells cost output.

solar-panel-cleaning.alt: Technician cleaning solar panels with a water-fed pole on a commercial rooftop
solar-panel-cleaning.caption: Purified water and a panel-safe brush — no detergent left on the glass to attract the next layer.

solar-panel-cleaning.alt: Solar panels after cleaning, with clear glass and no soap film or mineral residue
solar-panel-cleaning.caption: After, same rows. Dried without spotting.

solar-panel-cleaning.alt: Wide view of the full 128-panel array after a pure-water cleaning
solar-panel-cleaning.caption: After, the whole array.

solar-panel-cleaning.alt: Technician standing on a rooftop cleaning solar panels with a long-handled brush
solar-panel-cleaning.caption: Residential arrays get the same water and the same brush as the commercial ones.

solar-panel-cleaning.alt: Brush on a long pole cleaning wet solar panels, water streaking across the glass
solar-panel-cleaning.caption: The brush agitates; the purified water carries it off and dries clear.

solar-panel-cleaning.alt: Technician cleaning a rooftop solar array with a water-fed pole beside a single-storey home
solar-panel-cleaning.caption: Worked from the ground where the roof allows it — safer, and no foot traffic on the panels.

commercial-window-cleaning.alt: Cleaned storefront windows under blue awnings at a business
commercial-window-cleaning.caption: Storefront glass at a Whatcom County business. Commercial glass is judged from the pavement, in daylight.

commercial-window-cleaning.alt: Cleaned restaurant storefront windows and glass at a commercial location
commercial-window-cleaning.caption: A restaurant frontage on the same round.

moss-under-shingles.alt: Asphalt roof buried under thick moss, needles and forest debris before treatment
moss-under-shingles.caption: Before, Sedro-Woolley. This is what a shaded roof does under forest cover here.

moss-under-shingles.alt: Two skylights almost buried under leaves, needles and moss before the roof was cleared
moss-under-shingles.caption: Before. Both skylights are under there.

moss-under-shingles.alt: Gloved hand holding a thick clump of moss and organic debris lifted off a roof
moss-under-shingles.caption: Moss comes off by hand and at low pressure. A pressure washer takes the shingle granules with it.

moss-under-shingles.alt: Roof partway through moss removal, cleared shingles on one side and growth remaining on the other
moss-under-shingles.caption: Halfway across, which is the clearest look at what was actually on the roof.

moss-under-shingles.alt: Roof ridge after the bulk moss and debris were removed, with the shingles visible again
moss-under-shingles.caption: After. Same roof as the first photograph in this run.

overflowing-gutters.alt: Gutter and roof edge filled with fallen autumn leaves
overflowing-gutters.caption: What a gutter looks like when it is already past overflowing.

overflowing-gutters.alt: Gloved hand removing packed debris from a clogged gutter
overflowing-gutters.caption: Ferndale. Leaves, moss and grit compact into a plug that water runs straight over.

overflowing-gutters.alt: Close-up of a gray asphalt shingle roof meeting the gutter line
overflowing-gutters.caption: Sedro-Woolley. The roof edge and the gutter are one system, and they silt up together.

overflowing-gutters.alt: Gutter packed with fir needles and roof debris before the roof was cleared
overflowing-gutters.caption: Before. Under forest cover the roof and the gutter fill together, so they are one job rather than two.

overflowing-gutters.alt: Asphalt roof and gutter line covered in needles, leaves and organic debris
overflowing-gutters.caption: Before. A gutter in this state does not drip — it overflows at the back edge, behind the fascia.

overflowing-gutters.alt: Roof edge and gutter cleared of debris, with the shingle surface exposed
overflowing-gutters.caption: After, same roof edge.

north-facing-wall-mildew.alt: White lap siding before washing, with green organic growth across the lower courses
north-facing-wall-mildew.caption: Before, a Lynden home. Growth starts low and on the shaded side, where the wall stays damp longest.

north-facing-wall-mildew.alt: Long exterior wall of a home before washing, dulled by organic buildup
north-facing-wall-mildew.caption: Before. From here it reads as "the paint has aged", which is usually growth rather than age.

north-facing-wall-mildew.alt: Close-up of heavy green and dark organic staining embedded on white siding
north-facing-wall-mildew.caption: Close up, it is clearly biological — and it is in the surface, not on it.

north-facing-wall-mildew.alt: Technician applying a siding-safe soft wash solution to an upper wall
north-facing-wall-mildew.caption: Applied from the ground. Water driven behind a lap board has to come out somewhere.

north-facing-wall-mildew.alt: Technician soft washing the exterior wall of a home from the lawn at low pressure
north-facing-wall-mildew.caption: Siding gets washed, not blasted.

north-facing-wall-mildew.alt: Side wall of a home before washing, with organic discoloration along the siding
north-facing-wall-mildew.caption: Before, the shaded side wall.

slippery-driveways-and-walkways.alt: Large concrete area in front of a home, darkened almost black by organic growth
slippery-driveways-and-walkways.caption: Before, Mount Vernon. Concrete goes black here from organic growth, not dirt — which is why sweeping never touches it.

slippery-driveways-and-walkways.alt: Concrete before cleaning, showing the extent of dark organic contamination
slippery-driveways-and-walkways.caption: Before, the front entry. Black concrete is biological, and biological is what makes it slick underfoot.

slippery-driveways-and-walkways.alt: Technician running a surface cleaner across a driveway beside the branded company truck
slippery-driveways-and-walkways.caption: The truck carries its own water, tanks and power, so a job does not depend on the tap at the property.

slippery-driveways-and-walkways.alt: Technician running a professional surface cleaner across concrete beside the company truck
slippery-driveways-and-walkways.caption: A surface cleaner rather than a wand, so there are no stripes left across the slab.

slippery-driveways-and-walkways.alt: Concrete walkway showing the contrast between a cleaned section and darker untreated concrete
slippery-driveways-and-walkways.caption: Mid-job on the walkway. The line is the honest measure of what was on the surface.

slippery-driveways-and-walkways.alt: The concrete walkway after cleaning, organic growth and dark staining removed
slippery-driveways-and-walkways.caption: After. A walkway that goes black also goes slippery, which is the part that matters in a wet winter.

solar-output-dropped.alt: Wide view of a 128-panel commercial solar array on a flat rooftop
solar-output-dropped.caption: A 128-panel commercial array. Output is measurable, so on a roof this size so is the cost of leaving it dirty.

solar-output-dropped.alt: Rows of solar panels coated in dirt, dust and water spotting before cleaning
solar-output-dropped.caption: Before. Panels do not need to look filthy to be down on output.

solar-output-dropped.alt: Close-up of a solar panel showing heavy dirt, pollen and bird droppings on the glass
solar-output-dropped.caption: Pollen, dust and droppings. Any of it shades cells, and shaded cells cost output.

solar-output-dropped.alt: Technician cleaning solar panels with a water-fed pole on a commercial rooftop
solar-output-dropped.caption: Purified water and a panel-safe brush — no detergent left on the glass to attract the next layer.

solar-output-dropped.alt: Solar panels after cleaning, with clear glass and no soap film or mineral residue
solar-output-dropped.caption: After, same rows. Dried without spotting.

solar-output-dropped.alt: Wide view of the full 128-panel array after a pure-water cleaning
solar-output-dropped.caption: After, the whole array.

composition-asphalt-shingle.alt: High-angle view along a shingle roof ridge with a vent pipe, water beyond
composition-asphalt-shingle.caption: Composition shingle with the growth taken off it. The granules are the wearing surface.

standing-seam-metal-roof.alt: Standing-seam metal roof inspected and assessed before a low-pressure soft wash
standing-seam-metal-roof.caption: Assessed before anything is applied — coating condition decides what the roof can take.

vinyl-siding.alt: Close-up of lap siding before treatment, showing green organic growth across several boards
vinyl-siding.caption: Organic growth across lap boards, before a soft wash.

wash-water-and-storm-drains.alt: Technician protecting siding, windows and planting before soft washing a roof
wash-water-and-storm-drains.caption: Protecting what is below the work is the same discipline as controlling where the water goes.

before.alt: Large waterfront window before cleaning, heavy streaking and salt residue clouding the view
before.caption: Before. The streaking is mineral residue left behind as salt spray dries on the pane.

after.alt: The same waterfront window after cleaning, clear glass and an unobstructed view to the water
after.caption: After, same pane.

before.alt: Bank of green-framed waterfront windows before cleaning, hazy with salt spray
before.caption: Before. Salt haze does not rinse off in the rain — it has to be washed off, or it keeps dulling the view.

after.alt: Bank of green-framed windows after cleaning, glass and frames clear
after.caption: After, same bank of windows.

before.alt: Green-framed glass door and sidelight before cleaning, webs and dirt along the frames
before.caption: Before. Webs and debris collect in the frame channels, not only on the glass, which is why frames and tracks are part of the job.

after.alt: Green-framed glass door after cleaning, free of webs and debris
after.caption: After, same door. Frames and sill cleared as well as the glass.

before.alt: Asphalt roof and gutter line covered in needles, leaves and organic debris
before.caption: Before. A gutter in this state does not drip — it overflows at the back edge, behind the fascia.

after.alt: Roof edge and gutter cleared of debris, with the shingle surface exposed
after.caption: After, same roof edge.

before.alt: Asphalt roof buried under thick moss, needles and forest debris before treatment
before.caption: Before, Sedro-Woolley. This is what a shaded roof does under forest cover here.

after.alt: Roof ridge after the bulk moss and debris were removed, with the shingles visible again
after.caption: After. Same roof as the first photograph in this run.

before.alt: Two skylights almost buried under leaves, needles and moss before the roof was cleared
before.caption: Before. Both skylights are under there.

after.alt: The same skylights after debris removal, fully exposed on a cleared roof
after.caption: After, same skylights.

before.alt: Green standing-seam metal roof on a stone home before cleaning, dulled by organic growth
before.caption: Before, Whatcom County. The green finish is still under there; what you see is growth sitting on the coating.

after.alt: The stone home's metal roof after cleaning, with the green finish restored
after.caption: After, from the same position as the first photograph in this run.

before.alt: Side wall of a home before washing, with organic discoloration along the siding
before.caption: Before, the shaded side wall.

after.alt: The same side wall after soft washing, the white siding clean and uniform
after.caption: After, same wall, same day.

before.alt: Close-up of lap siding before treatment, showing green organic growth across several boards
before.caption: Before, close enough to count the courses.

after.alt: Close-up of lap siding after soft washing, clean and free of organic growth
after.caption: After, same boards.

before.alt: Long exterior wall of a home before washing, dulled by organic buildup
before.caption: Before. From here it reads as "the paint has aged", which is usually growth rather than age.

after.alt: The same long exterior wall after washing, with bright, clean siding
after.caption: After. Same wall as the second photograph in this run.

before.alt: Concrete before cleaning, showing the extent of dark organic contamination
before.caption: Before, the front entry. Black concrete is biological, and biological is what makes it slick underfoot.

after.alt: Front entry and concrete after pressure washing, visibly brighter and more uniform
after.caption: After, the front entry.

before.alt: Rows of solar panels coated in dirt, dust and water spotting before cleaning
before.caption: Before. Panels do not need to look filthy to be down on output.

after.alt: Solar panels after cleaning, with clear glass and no soap film or mineral residue
after.caption: After, same rows. Dried without spotting.
